previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted after experiencing post-procedural bleeding following a radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of a liver tumor in segment 7. A CT scan revealed arterial extravasation from the ablation tract, prompting transfer to the angiography suite. Angiography showed no active bleeding, and the patient was briefly hypotensive, requiring pressors and temporary intubation before stabilization. The procedure was terminated without treating two additional tumors in segment 8. He remained hemodynamically stable overnight with no further bleeding. His diuretics were held initially but restarted at discharge, and home medications were continued. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor for complications and follow up with oncology and hepatology in four weeks for treatment reassessment.
problems: Esophageal varices without mention of bleeding
